caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-20
attempts.entry_title: MEC head-direction cells on a rotating arena (Park, Keeley, Savin, Ranck and Fenton 2019)
attempts.summary: In this data the paper's core result holds: head-direction tuning in medial entorhinal cortex degrades during arena rotation, while firing rates and the sub-second coupling of cell pairs are preserved. The preservation of internally referenced tuning in cell pairs did not reproduce, nor did its short-lived registration to the arena frame; the Methods and the paper's code normalise this tuning differently, and the record asks which was used. The link between frame-specific directional information and proximity to the shock zones, and the structure of decoding errors, were weaker than reported. Learning, LFP and the analyses of all MEC cells could not be tested, as only the 115 head-direction cells are deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Park, Keeley, Savin, Ranck and Fenton (2019) on CRCNS data set hc-20, which holds the spike trains and 30 Hz tracking of 115 MEC head-direction cells from 13 rats in stable1, rotating (room and arena coordinates) and stable2 trials of the two-frame place avoidance task, with the tracker files of each trial. It ports the paper's maximum likelihood decoder and internally referenced tuning from its Python code, and tests directional tuning, its stability, Idir frame preference, cell-pair correlations and the decoding error distributions. The other MEC cells, the LFP and the training sessions are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Park et al. (2019) from CRCNS hc-20
Findings of attempt park-2019-01 checked on CRCNS hc-20 (unversioned)

outcomes.statement: The paper analyses 115 dorsal MEC head-direction cells from 13 rats, among 353 MEC cells forming 556 cell pairs (Table S1), out of 1594 MEC single units recorded.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1; STAR Methods, Electrophysiology; Table S1
outcomes.quote: We recorded 115 dorsal MEC head-direction cells (Figure S1; Table S1) from 13 rats
outcomes.notes: The data set holds 115 head-direction units from 13 rats, matching the paper's 115 from 13 rats; per rat they match Table S1 except R029 (40 against 41) and R523 (2 against 1), and both R523 units are named R523 in all their files. Applying the paper's criteria at p < 0.05 (reading b), with the Rayleigh test of the tuning curve's vector and n the spikes behind it, 110 of 115 pass; two units fire above 10 AP/s in stable1 (13.8 and 11.9), two have Kuiper p of 0.051 and 0.054, and three a Rayleigh p of 0.28 to 0.43 (two of them among the Kuiper failures). With n = 36 bins 83 pass, and with the Rayleigh test of the raw spike directions 110. Reading (b) is circular, as the deposited units were already selected as head-direction cells. The data set holds no other MEC units, so the 353 MEC cells and 556 MEC cell pairs of Table S1 cannot be counted; the measured values for them are the 115 units and the 146 simultaneously recorded pairs the data set holds, all head-direction cells. The paper analyses 142 head-direction pairs in Figure 4; 142 of the 146 have a defined 5 s internally referenced curve in every condition (fig4-internal-tuning-preserved), which may be how the paper counted them.
deviations: Spike width cannot be applied (no waveforms are deposited).
Units matched across trials by tetrode and cluster in the file names, as FileNameList.xlsx is shifted for five units of session 1121R157.

The n of the Rayleigh test of the tuning curve's vector is not stated (STAR Methods, Quantifying Head-direction Signals, Directionality, "converted to a z statistic"); it is taken as the number of spikes behind the curve, with n = 36 bins shown as a variant. The count under reading (a) does not depend on it.

outcomes.statement: The head-direction cells have long-duration spikes and a mean firing rate of 1.41 ± 0.20 AP/s.
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Data Analysis, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: MEC head direction cells were classified as cells with long duration action potentials (avg. width at 30% of the peak voltage 169.79 ± 4.58 ms) and average firing rate below 10 AP/s (avg. 1.41 ± 0.20 AP/s)
outcomes.notes: Mean stable1 rate 1.392 AP/s (reading a) and mean over three trials 1.433 AP/s (reading b), both within 1.41 ± 0.20. The median is 0.668 AP/s. Two units fire above 10 AP/s in stable1, the paper's stated upper limit. Spike width is not tested.

outcomes.statement: The 13 recorded rats learned the place avoidance task, with performance improving over trials in the stable (baseline) and the rotating (challenge) conditions and no trial by frame interaction in the rotating condition.
outcomes.source: Figure 1A legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: right: learning curves from the 13 recorded rats in the stable [baseline]

statistics.about: rotating condition, trial by frame interaction

outcomes.notes: The learning curves are over the pretraining and training sessions. The data set's 176 tracker files hold only the 44 recording sessions (stable1, rotating in room and arena coordinates, stable2), 1 to 12 per rat; the training sessions are not deposited, and the data descriptor does not mention them.

outcomes.statement: Rotation did not change locomotor speed relative to stable1, measured in either frame, but speed was lower in stable2 than in the other conditions.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, top left, and its legend
outcomes.quote: Effect of rotation on (top left) speed

statistics.test: repeated-measures ANOVA, Greenhouse-Geisser corrected, Tukey-Kramer HSD

outcomes.notes: Mean speed per session from the TSD positions (2.1333 pixels/cm). With the 40 sessions whose tracking is not duplicated, reading (a), successive samples, gives F(1.94, 75.59) = 64.80, p = 7.6e-17 (the paper F(2.02, 74.68) = 46.61); stable2 10.76 cm/s against 14.63 to 15.60 for the others, each adjusted p below 0.0001 by Tukey HSD on the repeated-measures error term, and stable1 and the two rotating frames do not differ (adjusted p 0.08 to 1.00); the between-groups Tukey-Kramer HSD gives the same (0.38 to 1.00). Reading (b), 1 s steps, F(1.87, 72.82) = 55.86, p = 6.9e-15, gives the pattern with the between-groups test (others adjusted p 0.07 to 0.84) but not with the repeated-measures error term, where the room and arena frames differ (adjusted p = 0.0045). Reading (a) gives the pattern under either error term. With all 44 sessions, reading (a) gives a room-arena difference at adjusted p = 0.048 on the repeated-measures error term.
deviations: The four sessions whose tracking duplicates another session's (1015R029, 1025R029, 1211R039, 1212R039) are left out of the main test, as one trial of each pair carries another day's tracking; they are kept in a variant.

Tukey HSD uses the repeated-measures error term of the ANOVA (an assumption; STAR Methods, Statistics, name Tukey-Kramer HSD after repeated-measures ANOVAs run in JMP), with the between-groups Tukey-Kramer HSD and paired t-tests as variants. The outcome is the same under both error terms (reading a).

outcomes.statement: Power in the MEC local field potential did not differ across conditions.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, top right, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Despite excellent navigation (Figure 1A), maintained firing rates, and power in the local field potential (LFP)
outcomes.notes: The data set holds no LFP; the zip holds only TSD spike and tracking files and tracker .dat files, and the data descriptor does not mention LFP.

outcomes.statement: Firing rates of the head-direction cells were maintained across stable1, rotating and stable2.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, bottom left, and its legend
outcomes.quote: Despite excellent navigation (Figure 1A), maintained firing rates
outcomes.notes: Mean rates 1.392, 1.710 and 1.198 AP/s in stable1, rotating and stable2; repeated-measures ANOVA with Greenhouse-Geisser correction (Mauchly p = 9.4e-17) F(1.35, 154.10) = 1.76, p = 0.184 (the paper F(1.34, 153.21) = 1.89, p = 0.17). Mean change +0.318 AP/s in rotation and -0.194 in stable2. Without the unit with the highest rotating rate (1001R523-P9C1, 40.1 AP/s in rotation, 7.8 in stable1) p = 0.275, and without it and 1024R157-P9C1 p = 0.29. Variants find differences, a Wilcoxon test of rotating against stable1 (p = 0.02) and the ANOVA on log rates (p = 0.0015), so the absence rests on the paper's test on raw rates.

outcomes.statement: Directional tuning of head-direction cells was strongly degraded during rotation in both frames, more in the arena frame than in the room frame, and returned in stable2 (stable1 = stable2 > rotating room frame > rotating arena frame).
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, bottom right, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: stable1 = stable2 > rotating-room frame > rotating-arena frame (p < 0.01; post hoc using Tukey-Kramer honest significant difference [HSD])
outcomes.notes: Directionality differs across conditions, F(2.77, 315.60) = 72.66, p = 8.9e-34 (the paper F(3, 342) = 70.36). Means 0.460 stable1, 0.421 stable2, 0.344 room, 0.170 arena. With Tukey HSD on the repeated-measures error term, stable1 and stable2 do not differ (p = 0.27), room is below stable1 (p below 0.0001) and stable2 (p = 0.0019), and arena is below room (p below 0.0001), every required pair at p < 0.01. With the between-groups Tukey-Kramer HSD (variant) room is not below stable2 at p < 0.01 (p = 0.055), which would make the outcome partial. Bonferroni-corrected paired t-tests agree with the main reading (stable2 against room p = 0.0048, stable1 against stable2 p = 0.14). The outcome was partially reproduced before the first verification round, with the between-groups test.
deviations: Greenhouse-Geisser applied, as Mauchly's test is significant (p = 0.0042); the paper's degrees of freedom, F(3, 342), are uncorrected.

Tukey HSD uses the repeated-measures error term of the ANOVA, an assumption. The STAR Methods (Statistics) name Tukey-Kramer HSD after repeated-measures ANOVAs run in JMP 12 without saying which error term, and the paper's F(3, 342) on 115 cells implies a within-cell error term. A between-groups HSD ignores that the four conditions are measured on the same cells. The outcome rests on this choice.

outcomes.statement: The change in preferred direction differs across trial pairs (stable1-stable2 = stable1-rotating room frame > stable1-rotating arena frame), and is greater for every trial pair than between the two halves of stable1.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D, left, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The rotation-induced change in (left) directional preference differs across trial pairs

statistics.about: trial pairs against the two halves of stable1
statistics.test: ANOVA, Dunnett's test against the stable1 halves

outcomes.notes: Trial pairs F(2, 228) = 17.80, p = 6.6e-08 (the paper F(2, 228) = 10.54); four groups F(3, 456) = 19.62, p = 5.6e-12 (the paper F(3, 456) = 15.38). Every trial pair exceeds the stable1 halves by Dunnett's test (p = 0.019, 0.0073, below 0.0001). Stable1-stable2 and stable1-room do not differ (58 and 60 degrees, Tukey p = 0.94 on the repeated-measures error term, 0.95 between groups), but stable1-arena is larger (91 degrees, p < 0.0001), where the legend orders it below the other two. The criterion makes this partial. Whether the legend's order is garbled, as the round 1 verifier suggested, is asked of a reader (questions/park-2019.yaml); the claim is tested as written.
deviations: Halves of stable1 are its first and second 15 min, as the claims file reads them.

outcomes.statement: Directional instability (the KLD between tuning curves) differs across trial pairs and is greater for every trial pair than between the two halves of stable1.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D, right, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: the change in preferred direction of directional tuning and the overall change in directional tuning (''instability'') was greater across the two stable conditions and between the stable and rotating conditions than it was between the two halves of the first stable session (Figure 1D)

statistics.about: trial pairs against the two halves of stable1
statistics.test: ANOVA, Dunnett's test against the stable1 halves

outcomes.notes: KLD on spike counts (reading a) gives trial pairs F(1.60, 182.42) = 11.74, p = 7.2e-05 (the paper F(1.62, 184.22) = 7.78) and four groups F(3, 456) = 13.74, p = 1.4e-08; stable1-stable2 and stable1-arena exceed the halves by Dunnett's test (p = 0.0044 and below 0.0001), but stable1-room does not (p = 0.13). KLD on rates (reading b) gives F(1.60, 182.29) = 8.47, p = 0.00084, four groups p = 0.0026, and only stable1-arena exceeds the halves (p = 0.0008). With the rates rescaled to the spike count before the Krichevsky-Trofimov estimate (a variant, as adding 0.5 to rates far below 1 flattens the probabilities) only stable1-arena exceeds the halves (p below 0.0001; the others 0.15 and 0.26). The criterion has no partial form; the outcome is partial because two of the three comparisons with the halves hold under reading (a). Read strictly, the claim is not reproduced.
deviations: The criterion gives only the reproduced form. Partially reproduced is a judgement outside it, made because both ANOVAs and two of the three comparisons with the halves hold under reading (a); this is an assumption, and under a strict reading of the criterion the outcome would be not reproduced.

outcomes.statement: Head direction decoded from stable1 ensemble tuning is relatively accurate in stable2 and relatively inaccurate and abruptly changing in both frames during rotation, although for some ensembles room-frame decoding is similar to stable2; seven ensembles of at least five head-direction cells were analysed.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 2; Figure 2A and 2B
outcomes.quote: Seven ensembles of R5 cells were analyzed ... Relatively accurate decoding of the stable2 recordings (Figure 2A) contrast with relatively inaccurate and abruptly changing decoding in both the room and arena spatial frames during rotation, although for some ensembles, decoding in the room frame was similar to decoding in the stable2 condition
outcomes.notes: Seven sessions hold at least five head-direction units (four of 6 and three of 5). With 20-sample windows the stable2 error is below the arena-frame error in 4 of 7 ensembles and below the room-frame error in 4 of 7, by the median and by the mean absolute error, and the same with 4-sample windows. Stable2 decoding is near or above chance (90 degrees) in 1026R157, 1117R157 and 1121R157 (medians 102 to 135), where decoding the second half of stable1 from its first half is also poor (65 to 116 degrees). Room is decoded better than arena in 6 of 7. The outcome rests on the claims file's majority rule (four of seven), which the paper does not give.
deviations: Windows without any tracked direction are dropped from training; the code would place them in the first bin.
The stable2 decoding of 1121R157 uses the first 15 min, as one of its stable2 files lasts 15 min.

outcomes.statement: During rotation, frame-specific directional discharge alternated between signaling room and arena direction; four of seven ensembles showed an overall room preference and two of seven an arena preference.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 3; Figure S2A and S2B; Figure 2C legend
outcomes.quote: 4/7 ensembles showed an overall preference to signal room directions over arena directions and 2/7 showed an overall preference to signal arena directions over room directions
outcomes.notes: Of the 16 readings the criterion names (bins 10 or 45 degrees, probabilities from the rotating trial or stable1, SD of the ΔIdir series or of stable1 Idir, no-preference margin a factor of 2 or both below 0.05), one gives 4 room- and 2 arena-preferring ensembles (45 degree bins, rotating-trial probabilities, ΔIdir SD, both below 0.05). The other 15 give 0 to 5 room and 0 to 1 arena; 14 of 16 give more room- than arena-preferring ensembles. Under the matching reading the room-preferring ensembles are 0930R029, 1004R029, 1022R029 and 1117R157 (p above 2 SD 0.605, 0.291, 0.199 and 0.054 against below 0.000, 0.000, 0.000 and 0.030) and the arena-preferring 1023R029 (0.000 against 0.367) and 1121R157 (0.041 against 0.061); two labels rest on differences of 0.02 to 0.03. The criterion reproduces the claim under any reading; the outcome rests on that one reading.
deviations: Idir is undefined where the observed count never occurs at that direction in the reference trial (only with stable1 probabilities); an interval where any cell's Idir is undefined is left out.
The direction of an interval is the circular mean of its tracked samples.

outcomes.statement: The rat's relative proximity to one shock zone versus the other is anti-correlated with frame-specific directional information, so that near the room shock zone directional discharge favours the arena frame and the reverse; this holds for Idir in each frame (mean r = -0.141 ± 0.029, all p < 0.0001) and for ΔIdir (r = -0.18, p < 0.05, in the exemplar).
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 2C and its legend; Figure S2C
outcomes.quote: This anticorrelation was observed for Idir defined for each spatial frame ... 0.141 ± 0.029; all p < 0.0001), as well as for their combination DIdir

statistics.about: Idir per frame against relative proximity, each ensemble
Idir against relative proximity, second report
ΔIdir against relative proximity, ensemble b

outcomes.notes: Under every reading (Idir bins and probabilities, proximity a or b, and distance to the zone's centre, to its nearest point, or by angle about the arena centre to the zone's centre direction) the mean of the 14 frame-specific correlations is negative, -0.043 to -0.087 (first reading -0.0698), and none of the 24 is within -0.141 ± 0.029 or -0.132 ± 0.024; 9 to 12 of 14 are negative and 7 to 11 negative with p < 0.0001, never all 14. ΔIdir correlates negatively with proximity at p < 0.05 in 4 to 6 of 7 ensembles (mean r -0.040 to -0.128). The criterion makes this partial under every reading, so the outcome does not rest on how the distance is measured.
deviations: The paper does not define the distance to a shock zone. Three are run, to the zone's centre (centre angle and mid radius from the tracker headers, angle counted with y up as the tracker's zone flags show), to its nearest point (0 inside), and the angle about the arena centre between the rat and the zone's centre direction. They give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: The frame preference ΔIdir does not vary systematically with head direction; its polar distribution over head direction in either frame is not biased toward the shock zones and does not differ from uniform.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 4; Figure S3 legend
outcomes.quote: did not significantly differ from uniform (average r = 0.17 ± 0.02; p > 0.17; Figure S3)
outcomes.notes: With 10 degree Idir bins and rotating-trial probabilities the average Rayleigh r is 0.166 (expected 0.17 ± 0.02). With n the sum of the weights no test of 14 is significant (smallest p = 0.35); with n the number of bins one is (1121R157 room frame, p = 0.014). The other Idir readings give average r 0.180 to 0.264 and 1 to 5 significant tests of 14. A question on the claims file asked whether every test should have p > 0.17, the bound the paper reports; the reader answered on 2026-11-13 that the criterion stands (non-significance at 0.05), so the answer changed nothing here and the claim was not re-run. With the assumed n the smallest p is 0.35, so the tests would also meet that bound. The 10 degree, rotating-trial Idir reading is not the only one under which figs2-frame-preference reproduces; that claim matches with 45 degree bins and rotating-trial probabilities, and under that Idir reading 1 of 14 tests here is significant even with n the sum of the weights (smallest p = 0.040), so the claim would not be reproduced under it.
deviations: The n of the weighted Rayleigh test is taken as the sum of the weights, the convention of the weighted Rayleigh test in CircStat (circ_rtest), the field's standard MATLAB toolbox; the paper does not say. With n the number of bins the claim is not reproduced (1 of 14 tests at p < 0.05). The Idir reading is the first the figs2 criterion lists, not the one under which figs2 reproduces (45 degree bins), where 1 of 14 tests is significant under either n. Both are assumptions the outcome rests on.

outcomes.statement: The sub-second temporal coupling of head-direction cell pairs (Kendall correlations of spike counts at 40, 250 and 1000 ms) was maintained across stable1, rotating and stable2.
outcomes.source: Figure 3B and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning and Maintained Temporal Coupling, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The three conditions did not differ at any of the timescales
outcomes.notes: 146 simultaneously recorded head-direction pairs; one-way ANOVA of the Fisher-transformed Kendall tau over the three trials F(2, 435) = 0.098, p = 0.907 at 40 ms, 0.329, p = 0.72 at 250 ms, 0.483, p = 0.617 at 1000 ms (the paper F(2, 420) = 0.097, 0.305, 0.44). Tau in stable1 correlates with tau in rotation at r = 0.85 to 0.97. A repeated-measures ANOVA, a variant, finds small differences at 250 and 1000 ms (p = 0.034 and 0.036), with stable2 lowest. The units of every session share their first timestamp in every trial (0 of 132 session trials differ), so each pair is binned on a common origin; session 1017R035, whose stable2 header states a first timestamp of 5, holds one unit and forms no pair.
deviations: 146 pairs where the paper's degrees of freedom imply about 141.
Counts binned from the spike times over each trial, not from the tracker samples.

outcomes.statement: Cell-pair discharge correlations among all 556 MEC cell pairs were preserved across trials (r² > 0.55 between the two stable trials and r² ≥ 0.52 between stable1 and rotating).
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning and Maintained Temporal Coupling, paragraph 1; Figure S4
outcomes.quote: these correlations were also preserved among all the MEC cell pairs that were recorded (n = 556 pairs), regardless of the spatial functional class of the cells (r2 > 0.55 across the two stable conditions; r2 R 0.52 across the first stable and rotating session; Figure S4)
outcomes.notes: The claim uses all 556 MEC cell pairs. The data set holds only the 115 head-direction units (115 files in each trial folder, all listed in FileNameList.xlsx); the other MEC units are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: The 115 conventionally identified head-direction cells also score high in head-direction information estimated by the Gaussian process tuning model among the 921 modelled MEC cells.
outcomes.source: Figure S5 legend
outcomes.quote: The conventionally-identified cells also scored high in head-direction information, which validates the model-based approach.
outcomes.notes: The claim compares the head-direction cells with the 921 modelled MEC cells, which are not deposited; only the 115 head-direction units are.

outcomes.statement: Cell-pair discharge correlations within the grid-tuned, position-tuned and speed-tuned subclasses of MEC cells are maintained across stable and rotating trials.
outcomes.source: Figure S6 legend
outcomes.quote: Cell-pair specific discharge correlations within subclasses of spatially-tuned cells are maintained across the stable and rotating sessions.
outcomes.notes: The grid, position and speed classes come from the 921 modelled MEC cells, which are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: The MEC head-direction cells showed no systematic tuning of firing rate to angular head velocity.
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: There was no systematic tuning of firing rate to angular velocity in these MEC head-direction cells (data not shown).
outcomes.notes: In stable1, 12 of 115 units correlate with signed angular velocity at p < 0.05 (binomial p = 0.013 against 5%) and 49 of 115 with unsigned angular velocity (p = 5.7e-33); rotating and stable2 give the same. The correlations are small (|r| at most 0.028 signed, 0.068 unsigned), and the sample-to-sample angular velocity reaches about 5400 degrees/s, which points to tracking noise. Tested against circular shifts of at least 30 s, which keep the serial dependence of the samples, 11 of 115 (binomial p = 0.029) and 41 of 115 (p = 3e-24) are significant, and after removing the head-direction bin means from both series 14 (p = 0.0019) and 34 (p = 1.8e-17), so the excess does not come from treating the samples as independent. The correlations are of both signs (49 to 53 of 115 positive for unsigned velocity) and at most 0.068 in size. The paper shows no data and names no test; the test is the claims file's assumption, and the outcome rests on it.
deviations: The test (per-unit Pearson correlation with angular velocity from successive samples, and a binomial test of the fraction significant) is the claims file's assumption; the paper names none. Stable1 is the main trial, as the classification trial; the others are variants.

outcomes.statement: Internally referenced directional tuning of head-direction cell pairs (tuning of one cell to head-direction displacement since the other's spikes) was preserved across stable1, rotating and stable2; neither its instability nor its change in preference differed between trials or from the two halves of stable1.
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 2; Figure 4B and 4D and the legend
outcomes.quote: Internally referenced tuning to head-direction displacement was preserved across the stable and rotating conditions

statistics.about: instability, trial pairs against stable1 halves
preference change, trial pairs against stable1 halves

outcomes.notes: Under the main readings (5 s, cell 2 spikes before the cell 1 spike, the Methods' normalisation; 142 pairs with a defined curve in every condition) instability differs across trial pairs, F(2.00, 282.00) = 10.20, p = 5.3e-05, and in the four-group ANOVA, F(3, 564) = 3.76, p = 0.011, and the preference change across trial pairs, F = 6.39, p = 0.0019; only the four-group preference test has p ≥ 0.05 (0.125). The differences are small (mean KLD 0.148 to 0.207 against 0.166 for the halves; stable1-room the largest). Of the eight readings, only 5 s, before, with the code's occupancy normalisation has all four at p ≥ 0.05. Its KLD is near 0 (means about 0.001), as the Krichevsky-Trofimov 0.5 swamps the normalised values; with the curve rescaled to its spike count (variant) that reading still has all four at p ≥ 0.05, the instability test at p = 0.052.
deviations: Cell 1 is the first-listed unit of each pair, as the code labels pairs i < j.
With the Methods' normalisation (a single number per curve) the curve is the spike-difference histogram; KLD uses its counts.

outcomes.statement: The strength of internally referenced directional tuning is similar in all conditions and frames for intervals up to 10 s, but beyond 10 s it falls in the rotating arena frame (20 to 60 s; stable1 = stable2 = rotating room > rotating arena) and at 300 to 600 s also in the rotating room frame (stable1 = stable2 > rotating room > rotating arena).
outcomes.source: Figure 4C and its legend; Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: during short intervals in the rotating condition, the strength of internally referenced directional tuning was similar in the two spatial frames but less so across longer intervals (Figure 4C). Specifically, internally referenced arena-frame tuning abruptly decreased after 10 s.

statistics.about: conditions at each interval up to 10 s
statistics.statistic: F(3, 564) ≤ 1.59 (printed with the glyph for ≥, read as ≤ since p > 0.19 at each interval)

statistics.about: conditions at each interval beyond 10 s
statistics.statistic: F(3, 564) ≥ 23.73 (printed with the glyph for ≤, read as ≥ since p < 10^-14 at each interval)

outcomes.notes: Run under the four readings of window side and normalisation. With the Methods' normalisation and cell 2 spikes before, the conditions do not differ at 3, 4 and 5 s (p = 0.13, 0.17, 0.11) but do at 10 s (p = 0.0086); with cell 2 spikes after they differ at 5 s (p = 0.020) and 10 s (p = 0.0024); with the code's normalisation they do not differ up to 10 s with cell 2 before (p = 0.096 to 0.50) and differ at 10 s with cell 2 after (p = 0.0094). Every reading differs at every interval beyond 10 s (p below 0.002). The arena frame is below all three other conditions at none of 20 to 60 s with the Methods' normalisation, and only at 60 s (before) or 50 and 60 s (after) with the code's. With the Methods' normalisation the room frame falls as far as or further than the arena frame at 20 to 50 s (before, 40 s, 0.267 and 0.281 against 0.410 and 0.452). With the code's normalisation the room frame falls first (cell 2 before, below both stable trials at 20 s, where the arena frame is not), and the arena frame is lower from 40 s (0.180 against 0.204 before, 0.181 against 0.208 after) and below the room frame by Tukey's test from 50 s (after) or 60 s (before). At 300 and 600 s the arena frame is below the others in every reading, and the room frame below both stable trials with the Methods' normalisation, as reported, but not at 600 s with the code's. The code's normalisation with cell 2 before meets the words of the partial form (no difference up to 10 s, differences at every later interval, the arena frame below the other three at 60, 300 and 600 s, the room frame not below stable2 at 600 s). The outcome takes "beyond 10 s" in the partial form as from 20 s, the arena-frame part of the full criterion, and under that reading no reading of window side and normalisation meets it; read as any interval beyond 10 s, the outcome would be partially reproduced. The outcome was partially reproduced before the first verification round, when only cell 2 spikes before were run; the verifier gave not reproduced.
deviations: Strength is the Rayleigh vector length of the internally referenced curve, the reading the claims file gives.
One-way ANOVA on 141 to 146 pairs per interval (pairs with a defined curve in all four conditions at that interval), with between-groups Tukey-Kramer HSD, as the criterion's one-way ANOVA implies.

The partial form ("the arena frame falls below the others beyond 10 s and not before, but the room-frame order at long intervals is not found") is read as requiring the arena-frame order of the full criterion, below the three others from 20 s, since it names only the room-frame order as missing, and the paper writes that arena-frame tuning "abruptly decreased after 10 s" while the ensemble registered to the room frame within about 10 s (Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 3). This is an assumption the outcome rests on.

outcomes.statement: The angular distribution of decoding error is inhomogeneous in the room frame (resultant r = 0.589) and the arena frame (r = 0.653) and differs from the distribution of sampled head directions, which is itself biased in both frames (r = 0.147 room, r = 0.378 arena).
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 4; Figure 5A and 5B and the legend
outcomes.quote: The angular distribution of the decoded directional error was not homogeneous in the room frame (Figure 5A; resultant vector r = 0.589; Rayleigh’s test; z = 236.36; p = 0.000); nor was the error distribution similar to the head-direction distribution
outcomes.notes: A reader amended the criterion on 2026-11-13 in answer to a question (questions/park-2019.yaml) so that it names three readings of what the error distribution is over, (i) mean absolute error per 10 degree head-direction bin, (ii) head directions of windows decoded within 15, 30 or 45 degrees, (iii) the signed error angles. Before the answer only (iii) was run. The claim was re-run under all three with the three pooling readings and both windows. Every test holds (all four distributions non-uniform, both Kuiper's tests at p < 0.05) in 75 of 80 combinations, but none has all four r within tolerance; the most is two. With the six-cell ensemble 0930R029 (reading b) and 20-sample windows, the room-frame r is 0.604 under reading (ii) at 15 degrees, 0.555 at 30 degrees and 0.560 under reading (iii), within tolerance of 0.589, and the arena-frame head-direction r is 0.360 (0.378); the arena-frame r is 0.484, 0.543 and 0.144 (0.653) and the room-frame head-direction r 0.072 (0.147). The measured values are those of reading (ii) at 15 degrees, the first listed reading with two r within tolerance. Reading (i) gives error r of 0.031 to 0.426 at 20 samples. Pooled (reading a) no r is within tolerance under any reading, and the medians over ensembles (reading c) reach at most 0.348 (room, reading ii at 666 ms) and 0.548 (arena, reading ii at 133 ms). The answer brings the arena-frame error r closer to 0.653 but not within tolerance, and leaves the outcome as it was under reading (iii) (partially reproduced, with measured values 0.560, 0.144, 0.0718 and 0.360). Four ensembles tie at six cells; the other three match at most one value under any reading. The paper's z values imply about 681 and 679 windows for the error distributions and 10,671 and 1,072 samples for the head-direction distributions; no row has both error counts within 10% of 681 and 679, and no ensemble or sum of ensembles matches the head-direction counts of both frames, so the paper's pooling cannot be recovered from the counts.
deviations: For reading (i) the paper does not give the n of the Rayleigh test; it is taken as the number of decoded windows, as the paper's z = 236.36 at r = 0.589 implies about 680, and n = 36 bins is shown as a variant (which leaves the arena-frame error uniform for every ensemble). Neither choice changes the outcome, which readings (ii) and (iii) also give.

For reading (i) Kuiper's test compares the error weights with the head-direction occupancy over the same 10 degree bins, with n the number of windows on each side; the paper does not say how the test was applied to this reading.

outcomes.statement: The room-frame decoding error histogram has strong minima at 110 and 350 degrees in the room frame, the directions of the leading edges of prominent orienting cues given the clockwise rotation; the minima correspond to the cue edges in the room frame but not in the arena frame.
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 4; Figure 5C and 5D
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, the room frame direction decoding error distribution showed strong minima at 110 ... in the room frame, which, given the clockwise arena rotation, are the directions at which the leading edges of prominent orienting cues were located
outcomes.notes: With the seven ensembles pooled and 20-sample windows, the mean absolute room-frame error by room-frame head direction (reading a) has its two deepest minima in the bins starting at 100 and 340 degrees (centres 105 and 345), within 10 degrees of 110 and 350 by their bin centres. This is 1 of 32 combinations of window, pooling and reading, against 0.20 expected by chance for two minima placed at random; 10 others find one of the two minima (6.6 expected by chance) and the pooled reading (a) with 133 ms windows finds neither. Were the 32 rows independent, at least one would match both minima by chance with probability 0.18 (they share data, so this is rough). The pooled curve is shallow (Rayleigh r 0.032 under fig5-error-inhomogeneous reading i; mean error 63.2 to 91.3 degrees by head direction, mean 76.8), and the two minima lie 13.6 and 13.4 degrees below the mean but only 0.1 and 1.6 degrees below their lower neighbouring bin, so the match is weak support. The outcome rests on the pooled reading. Whether the minima match the cue positions cannot be tested.
deviations: The paper does not say which recordings are pooled or which measure Figure 5C plots; the match is found with all seven ensembles pooled and the mean error by head direction, an assumption the outcome rests on.
The decoded direction is the start of the winning bin, as in the code, which biases the signed error by about -5 degrees; minima are located by their bin centres.

findings.statement: The data set holds only the 115 head-direction units. The other MEC units of the paper (353 cells and 556 pairs in Table S1, 921 modelled cells in Figures S5 and S6), the LFP, the waveforms and the pretraining and training sessions are not deposited, so the claims of Figures 1A, 1C (LFP), S4, S5 and S6 cannot be tested.

In FileNameList.xlsx the stable2 column of session 1121R157 is shifted by one row for five units (P11C2 to P9C3); each is listed with the next unit's stable2 file, and the last with 1121SA2R157-cl1.P11C2Rm. The spike counts confirm the shift (P11C2 has 327 spikes in stable1, 52 in rotation, and is listed with a stable2 file of 21567).

Two pairs of trials from different days carry identical tracking (positions and directions, sample for sample) with different spikes. Stable2 of 1015R029 and of 1025R029, and the room-frame rotating trial of 1211R039 and of 1212R039, whose arena-frame tracking differs. One trial of each pair holds another day's tracking.

The stable1 TSD file of unit 1024R157-P9C1 holds the same spikes, sample for sample, as its rotating-trial files (2919 spikes), on stable1 tracking; its stable1 spike train is very likely the rotating trial's.
The header of 1017SA2R035-cl.P11C2Rm states a sampling rate of 2000 samples/s and a first timestamp of 5; the file holds 54,185 samples, a 30 min trial at 30 Hz.
The spike times of 1020RAR157-cl.P11C1 (room and arena files) decrease once, by 1.5 ms.
The stable2 file 1121SA2R157-cl1.P11C2Rm holds 26,954 samples (15 min), where every other trial file holds about 54,000 (30 min).
Samples without a tracked direction (direction 4294967295, that is -1, 4 to 73% of a file's samples) and without a position (x = y = 0) are not described in the data descriptor.

The data descriptor does not say that the tracker's shock zone angles are counted with y pointing up (pixel y grows downwards), nor that spike times run ahead of the nominal sample times (first timestamp plus index over rate) by up to about 3 s within a trial, so the tracker samples are not evenly spaced at the stated rate.

The per-rat counts of head-direction units differ from Table S1 for R029 (40 in the data set, 41 in the table) and R523 (2 against 1); the totals agree (115). Both R523 units (session 1001R523, P1C1 and P9C1) are named R523 in all their files, so the files do not show which unit the table counts under another rat. Two deposited units fire above 10 AP/s in stable1 (13.8 and 11.9 AP/s), above the paper's stated limit for head-direction cells.

The tracker file 0803SA2R024RoomTrack_Room_20150803_153906.dat belongs to the session of rat R027 on 0803 (the other three trial files and the TSD files are R027), and 1007SA1R29RoomTrack... drops the leading zero of R029.

The paper reports 142 simultaneously recorded head-direction pairs; the 115 deposited units form 146. 142 of them have a defined 5 s internally referenced curve in every condition, which may be the count the paper used.

In sessions 1009R029, 1015R029, 1023R029 and 1025R029 the room-frame and arena-frame TSD tracks of the rotating trial disagree in distance from the arena centre (median 6.85 to 13.49 px at the best constant lag), while the session's room and arena .dat files agree (0.31 px), as the two TSD frames of 1022R029 do (0.31 px). Against the room .dat track the TSD tracks fall behind more and more through the trial, by 705 to at least 1500 samples in the room frame and 354 to 828 samples in the arena frame at sample 48000, so the spikes cannot be aligned with both frames.

reconciliation.blind_note: The author's first run saw nothing of park-2019-01, and all 17 of its first findings and the figs3 outcome were written then. In the author-answers run it printed questions/park-2019.yaml, which the answer run had copied from main and which held the two questions of park-2019-01 with that attempt's results (fig5 error r of 0.014 to 0.211, one of 14 figs3 tests at p = 0.0134 with n the number of bins), and the first lines of the author-answers and author-revise-3 reports of park-2019-01, left in transcripts/park-2019 (figs3 changed to not_reproduced, the outcomes of fig1c-speed, fig4-internal-tuning-preserved and no-angular-velocity-tuning, and the topics of its two methods_unavailable findings, among them the Tukey error term). In author-revise-2 it read the round 3 verifier report of park-2019-01 (figs3 not reproduced with n the number of bins) and said so in its report. It kept figs3 as reproduced, and the one finding added after these runs (number 15, on the Tukey error term) answers point 1 of its own round 1 verifier.

outcomes.note: A difference in method between the two notebooks, the n of the weighted Rayleigh test, which the criterion leaves open. Both find an average r of 0.166 and one test of 14 below 0.05 with n the number of bins (1121R157, room frame, p = 0.0134 and 0.014). The earlier attempt took n as the number of bins (reading a) and the blind one as the sum of the weights (reading b, as in CircStat), under which no test is significant.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed (one fig1d conclusion cell, whose heading did not begin "**Result:", was left in), the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier checked the archive's file list for the blocked claims and tested rayleigh_p, kuiper_two_sample, kld, rm_anova, internal_tuning and the decoder on synthetic inputs. It had no attempt record.

disagreements.reason: Under (a), p = 0.0086 at 10 s. At 20–60 s the room frame falls as much as or more than the arena frame; at 20 s arena > room. Under (b), the room frame falls first (20 s) and the arena frame is below the room frame only from 60 s. Neither normalisation shows the claimed room-preserved pattern. The "after" window side was computed only for 5 and 30 s, though the criterion asks for the window-side readings of fig4.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The full executed notebook after the first revision, with its conclusion cells and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the README and this attempt record, with the paper's full text.

disagreements.reason: The criterion has no partial form, and the record says so. Partial is therefore a judgement outside the criterion (the verifier made the same one in round 1). Either mark it assumed with that reason, or give not reproduced.

The n = sum-of-weights assumption is stated and is reasonable (CircStat convention). Not stated is that the Idir reading used (10 degree bins) is not the only one under which figs2 reproduces (45 degree bins, rotating trial, ΔIdir SD, both below 0.05). Under the figs2 reading figs3 has 1 of 14 tests significant even with n = sum of weights (min p 0.039, cell 48), so it would not reproduce. The record should say so.

The outcome depends on how "beyond 10 s" is read, and the record does not state that as an assumption. The before-side, code-normalisation reading meets the partial clause word for word (no differences up to 10 s, p < 0.05 at every later interval, arena below all three others at 60, 300 and 600 s, room not below stable2 at 600 s). Both 50 and 60 s are beyond 10 s, and "after the room frame" is not a condition in the criterion. Not reproduced is defensible if "beyond 10 s" is read as "from 20 s", which fits the paper's "abruptly decreased after 10 s" and its legend's 20 to 60 s order; the verifier's round-1 outcome made the same reading. Either mark it assumed and state that reading, or change it to partially reproduced. Separately, "at 20 to 50 s the room frame falls as far as or further than the arena frame" holds only with the Methods' normalisation; with the code's the arena frame is lower at 40 s (0.180 against 0.204 before, 0.181 against 0.208 after) and at 50 s.

paper_notes.statement: For Idir and ΔIdir (Figure 2C, S2, S3), the paper does not give the direction bins, the trial from which p(n|d) and p(n) are estimated, which SD the 2 SD rule uses, or the margin for no frame preference. The 4 room and 2 arena counts are found under 1 of 16 readings. Which were used?

Relative proximity to the shock zones (Figure 2C) is not defined. Is it a normalised difference of distances to the zones, and measured to the zone centre, its nearest edge or by angle? Here none of 24 readings gives the reported mean r of -0.141.

For the Rayleigh test of the normalised ΔIdir over head direction (Figure S3), is n the number of bins or the sum of the weights? With n the number of bins one of 14 tests is significant here (p = 0.014); with the sum of weights none is.

Tukey-Kramer HSD followed repeated-measures ANOVAs (Figure 1C, 1D). Did the post hoc tests use the repeated-measures error term? For directionality the room frame against stable2 gives p = 0.0019 with it and p = 0.055 between groups, which decides the outcome here.

For internally referenced tuning (Figure 4), the Methods normalise the histogram by the sum of the time offsets and the code by the occupancy of each displacement; the strength measure of Figure 4C is not defined; and the Methods do not say on which side of the cell 1 spike the cell 2 spikes are taken. Which normalisation and strength measure were used? Under the Methods' normalisation the trial-pair differences of Figure 4D are significant here (p = 5.3e-05 for instability).

Which decoded windows are pooled in the Figure 5 error distributions (the Rayleigh z values imply about 680 windows), and which measure Figure 5C plots (error by head direction, or the signed error histogram)?

The decoding window is 660 ms in the STAR Methods (20 samples of 33 ms, and num_samps = 20 in HD_Max_likelihood.py, 666 ms at the tracker's 30.02 samples/s) and 133 ms in the Figure 2 legend. The arena-frame error z is 289.63 in the Results and 153.24 and 230.58 in the Figure 5 legend, the z values the legend gives for the head-direction distributions.

entries.name: park-2019
entries.title: MEC head-direction cells on a rotating arena (Park, Keeley, Savin, Ranck and Fenton 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Park, Keeley, Savin, Ranck and Fenton (2019) on CRCNS data set hc-20, which holds the spike trains and 30 Hz tracking of 115 MEC head-direction cells from 13 rats in stable1, rotating (room and arena coordinates) and stable2 trials of the two-frame place avoidance task, with the tracker files of each trial. It ports the paper's maximum likelihood decoder and internally referenced tuning from its Python code, and tests directional tuning, its stability, Idir frame preference, cell-pair correlations and the decoding error distributions. The other MEC cells, the LFP and the training sessions are not in the data set.
